newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia seeks to reduce trade deficit with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australia seeks to reduce trade deficit with U.S..

text.p: Australia will try to reduce barriers blocking access to U.S. markets in an effort to even out the country's largest bilateral trade imbalance, Trade Minister Tim Fischer said Tuesday.

Fischer, who is also deputy prime minister, said he would hold further talks with U.S. Trade Representative-designate Charlene Barshefsky this year, although he said some progress had been made on access barriers.

"We remain concerned about the Export Enhancement Programme for grain subsidisation and the DEIP (Dairy Export Incentive) programme," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "There are still areas of great difficulty which we will continue to negotiate on."
Australia recorded a deficit in its merchandise trade balance with the United States in 1995-1996 of $12.97 billion Australian, or $10.1 billion U.S..
"There are cyclical and other structural reasons associated with that, but I am not happy about it and we would want to further expand our export effort to the U.S.," Fischer said.
The imbalance would level out rapidly without trade barriers, he said, adding that the Australian and U.S. governments enjoyed a particularly good bilateral relationship.
"I do not see insurmountable problems, but it is the speed at which some of these problems are addressed which is always very pertinent, very relevant," he said.
